verdict.root_cause: A platform-automation traffic-shaping container was attached to cart-service's network namespace ~3 minutes before onset, imposing a fixed 300ms egress delay with zero jitter on eth0, still in effect at onset [tr_c7c9b3c55cd2]. Every packet leaving cartservice — Redis commands to redis-cart and gRPC responses to callers — pays that fixed cost. Traces match exactly: each Redis HGET/HMSET takes ~300ms, AddItem (two commands) ~603-614ms, and callers see an extra ~300ms per call beyond the server span, tightly clustered in multiples of 300ms rather than spread as a tail [tr_2e2f3e84e02a]. Nothing errors — cartservice serves cart operations continuously with no error lines [tr_cd4598047f5c] and checkoutservice completes orders end to end, only slower [tr_e3a2c741032c]. The failure is injected wait time on cartservice's network path, propagating to checkout and the frontend edge.
verdict.reasoning: Two independent lines converge on the same quantity. The change record names a 300ms fixed-delay, zero-jitter egress shaper on cartservice's namespace three minutes before onset [tr_c7c9b3c55cd2]; traces show a latency floor quantised in exactly ~300ms units with no tail spread, the signature of injected delay rather than contention [tr_2e2f3e84e02a]. That result also rules out cartservice handler logic, other checkout dependencies (all sub-20ms), and a caller-specific client fault, since the frontend path shows the same gap. Class is dependency_latency, not bad_config: the shaper names no wrong address or limit, it inserts delay, and the service fails because it waits. Blame lands on cartservice because the shaper sits in its namespace and the delay appears on both its egress to Redis and its responses to two distinct callers. Competing near-onset changes are excluded by timing — the hotfix image reverted ~13m before onset, REDIS_ADDR:6380 reverted ~1.2h before [tr_c7c9b3c55cd2].
open_questions: No latency or request-rate metric was ever queried; the only query run was an error-ratio template returning no samples in either window, so the ~300ms step and its onset boundary were never confirmed against a time series [tr_c247e766f80d, tr_0a0db308b3f9].

Why the checkout→cartservice gap is ~3×300ms while the frontend gap is ~1×300ms is unsettled — connection-pool serialization is a hypothesis, not a finding [tr_2e2f3e84e02a]; and it is unconfirmed whether the shaper is still attached now.

Both log dispatches returned only the oldest 8 and newest 32 lines, leaving the onset interval itself unobserved [tr_cd4598047f5c, tr_e3a2c741032c]; redis-cart was never dispatched on directly, and 10 of 12 blast-radius services were not investigated.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow, adding ~300ms per cart command, with the shaping container coincidental.
alternatives.why_not: The ~300ms penalty also appears outside the Redis child spans, on the cartservice-to-caller leg for both frontend and checkout [tr_2e2f3e84e02a]; a slow Redis cannot explain that gap, and the zero-jitter quantisation matches a fixed shaper plus a change three minutes before onset [tr_c7c9b3c55cd2].

proposal.expected_effect: Reverting cartservice's configuration and recreating the container should detach the traffic-shaping attachment (eth0 delay=300ms) and remove the fixed egress delay. Measured in Jaeger, the only quantitative source that works here since Prometheus returns no samples for cartservice: Redis HGET/HMSET child spans fall from the tight ~300ms cluster to single-digit ms; cartservice server handlers fall from ~301-308ms (GetCart/EmptyCart) and ~603-614ms (AddItem) to tens of ms; the client-minus-server gap disappears (frontend GetCart client ~603-616ms, checkout EmptyCart client ~1205-1221ms both collapse toward server span). Corroborating: checkoutservice PlaceOrder->payment->email stage gaps return from ~1s to tens of ms, with orders still succeeding and no error lines.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if fresh traces 3-5 min after the recreate still show ~300ms Redis spans and the same 300ms multiples - meaning the delay is not in the reverted config (shaper attached out-of-band and surviving recreate, or redis-cart itself slow; redis-cart was never queried directly). Also sample traces immediately before acting: it is unconfirmed the shaper is still attached, and platform-automation removed it on its own once before, so a spontaneous recovery could be misread as a fix. If cart calls start erroring after the revert, the restored config is not the pre-shaper state.
proposal.risk: The change history is untrusted and shows five image update/revert pairs plus a REDIS_ADDR set/revert; 'previous configuration' may restore a stale REDIS_ADDR (redis-cart:6380) or hotfix image rather than the baseline in effect at onset, turning a latency incident into a cart outage. The recreate also discards in-process cache and drops in-flight gRPC calls. If the 300ms actually originates at redis-cart, this changes nothing and costs a restart.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice alone is modified, but its inbound callers see connection resets during the recreate: frontend (cart page and AddItem paths) and checkoutservice (PlaceOrder, which calls GetCart and EmptyCart), and through checkoutservice the order flow visible to loadgenerator. redis-cart sees cart traffic pause then resume at full rate.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Multiple services across the checkout path alerted within seconds of each other and propagated to the frontend and load generator, which is not a world that is working. Cartservice and checkoutservice alerting together first suggests a shared downstream dependency, but that is only a prior.
